headline: CISA adds actively exploited Perforce Puppet RCE flaw CVE-2026-115731 to KEV
summary: The Hacker News: CISA has added CVE-2026-115731 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing reports of active exploitation. headline: At least 178 major websites served malware via an Optimizely-related weakness
summary: KrebsOnSecurity reports that at least 178 major websites served data-stealing malware to visitors over a 24-hour period through a weakness involving Optimizely. Sites named include the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom. Experts said weak controls on third-party content sources made the incident worse.

headline: Microsoft agent-framework PyPI package compromised to deliver cloud credential stealer
summary: Multiple security vendors report that malicious versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package were published on November 17, 2026. The versions run a credential stealer every time Python starts and target cloud credentials. Any environment that installed these versions should be treated as potentially exposed.

summary: Socket reports that agent-framework versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 on PyPI were compromised. The malicious releases use .pth startup hooks to steal Azure, GitHub Actions and CI/CD credentials.

headline: Optimizely abused in supply-chain attack injecting malicious JavaScript into major websites
summary: Attackers used the Optimizely experimentation platform to push malicious JavaScript into high-profile websites. Visitors received cryptocurrency clippers, card skimmers and iOS malware. The exact compromise path has not been fully detailed.

headline: Cyberattack disrupts internal IT services at Norwegian energy company Equinor
summary: Equinor is working to contain a cyberattack on its IT systems that has disrupted internal services. The company says oil and gas production has not been affected. No attacker or attack method has been disclosed.

headline: Censys sinkholes domains in website supply-chain poisoning campaign pushing iOS exploits
summary: Censys saw visitors' browsers on popular websites contacting newly registered malicious domains, and began sinkholing those domains on 16 November 2026. The campaign, which Censys tracks as MCH and Caishen, delivered iOS exploits through poisoned web content. Hudson Rock first reported it.

headline: Malicious code delivered via Optimizely hits visitors to hundreds of websites
summary: Malicious code served through the third-party platform Optimizely reached visitors of hundreds of websites. The payloads reportedly include cryptocurrency-stealing malware and iOS exploits.

headline: Optimizely-delivered malware exposed visitors of at least 178 organizations
summary: At least 178 organizations, including several major brands, unknowingly served malware to their website visitors through the Optimizely platform. The incident shows how third-party web vendors can spread compromise across many sites at once.

headline: Optimizely confirms breach that injected malicious JavaScript into 178 customer websites
summary: Researchers found malicious JavaScript on 178 widely visited websites that run through the Optimizely Web experimentation platform. Optimizely has confirmed the breach. The source does not say what the code was designed to do or which sites were affected.

headline: CISA urges immediate patching of AI-discovered Java4Shell vulnerability
summary: CISA issued an alert urging organizations to patch Java4Shell right away. Experts warn the bug could let attackers take over servers without credentials and that it touches most of the Fortune 500. The report does not confirm exploitation.

headline: Critical OpenJDK 'Java4Shell' flaw could enable remote code execution in Java apps; CISA urges mitigations
summary: A critical vulnerability in OpenJDK, dubbed Java4Shell, could expose major Java applications to remote code execution. CISA has urged organizations to apply mitigations. The source does not report exploitation in the wild or give a CVE identifier.

headline: Critical unauthenticated RCE "Java4Shell" in OpenJDK runtime (CVE-2026-114938)
summary: Qualys ThreatPROTECT: Qualys reports a critical flaw in the OpenJDK runtime, CVE-2026-114938, that can let unauthenticated attackers execute code remotely. Because it sits in the runtime itself, services may be exposed even if their applications and libraries are not flawed. The advisory's URL refers to threat actors exploiting it, but the summary gives no exploitation details, so this needs verification. GreyNoise Blog: GreyNoise is monitoring scanning and exploitation attempts against the Java4Shell OpenJDK Base64 decoder flaw. Observed attempts show attacker interest, but the source does not confirm any successful compromise. Qualys Vulnerabilities and Threat Research: Qualys details Java4Shell, a memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder rated 9.2 (CVSS v4) by researchers and 8.1 (CVSS v3.1) by Oracle. Unauthenticated attackers may corrupt heap memory, leak secrets and achieve remote code execution; researchers demonstrated pre-auth RCE. Cisco Talos, CERT-EU Security Advisories: On 17 November 2026, Oracle and the OpenJDK project released fixes for CVE-2026-114938. Talos reports a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 for the flaw. It could allow unauthenticated remote code execution under certain conditions. The sources do not report exploitation in the wild. Help Net Security: Oracle and the OpenJDK project patched CVE-2026-114938, a memory corruption bug in the Base64 decoder that could let unauthenticated attackers run code on servers hosting Java applications. Researchers say exploitation is tricky and depends on specific CPUs. There is no evidence of successful attacks yet, but CISA urges organizations to patch immediately. The Hacker News: Oracle planned to release patches on November 17, 2026 for 11 Java SE vulnerabilities. All can be exploited remotely without authentication, with a maximum CVSS score of 8.1. Separate reports describe a potentially critical OpenJDK remote code execution flaw; no exploitation has been reported. Amazon Linux Security Center: A memory-corruption flaw in the OpenJDK Base64 decoder affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later on x86-64 systems with certain CPU capabilities; ARM64 is not affected. Depending on the deployment, it could let unauthenticated users crash the JVM or, in some environments, let an authenticated low-privileged user run code. Oracle has patched versions 17, 21, 25 and 27, and no exploitation has been reported.

summary: A critical OpenJDK vulnerability called Java4Shell may let unauthenticated attackers execute code on popular Java-based enterprise applications. Named affected products include Jenkins, Atlassian Jira, Confluence and Keycloak. The report does not confirm active exploitation.

headline: Oracle patches critical Java memory-corruption flaw enabling server takeover
summary: Researchers, helped by AI tooling, found a critical memory-corruption flaw in Java/OpenJDK. A short input string can reportedly trigger it and give attackers control of servers running Java. Oracle released a patch this week. The source does not report exploitation in the wild.

headline: Star Blizzard uses stolen identities from earlier breach to phish and compromise a US organization
summary: The Russian APT group Star Blizzard used data and identities stolen in late 2025 to pose as an employee of a firm it had already hacked. Using that disguise, it phished and compromised another US organization.

headline: Java4Shell flaw (CVE-2026-114938) enables pre-auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak on AVX-512 VBMI CPUs
summary: The Hacker News: Research firm Calif disclosed Java4Shell, a Java flaw that it says lets unauthenticated attackers run code on Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and three other widely used applications. The vulnerable code is in Java 17.0.6 and later, and it only runs on x86-64 Intel and AMD processors that support AVX-512 VBMI. The source does not report any exploitation in the wild. The Hacker News: CISA is urging organizations to patch CVE-2026-114938 right away. The newly disclosed Oracle Java flaw is an out-of-bounds write rated CVSS 8.1. Under certain conditions it can cause denial of service or remote code execution.

headline: Java4Shell: critical OpenJDK flaw allows unauthenticated code execution
summary: Security.NL reports a critical OpenJDK Java flaw named Java4Shell. It can let unauthenticated attackers run code in Java environments. The source gives no CVE ID and does not report exploitation.

headline: Google patches about 200 Chrome vulnerabilities, including several that could enable malware
summary: Google has fixed about two hundred vulnerabilities in Chrome. According to the source, several of them could let an attacker get malware onto a system. The source does not report active exploitation.

summary: Researchers at Calif demonstrated remote code execution in Jira, Jenkins and Keycloak through a Java vulnerability dubbed Java4Shell. VulnCheck says real-world exploitation requires work tailored to each target. No in-the-wild exploitation is reported in the source.

summary: Oracle's November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update includes 655 security patches across many product families, some covering third-party components. summary: Mandiant and GTIG report that Cold Relic, formerly tracked as COLDRIVER and UNC4057, compromised the cloud environment of a US organization in 2026. The group then used the stolen data to compromise a third party. This shows how one cloud intrusion can lead to linked intrusions at other organizations.

headline: Cursor links malicious Claude Code extension to compromised key issued to Fireworks
summary: Cursor reports that a malicious Claude Code extension traces back to a third-party breach. Threat actors used a compromised key issued to AI infrastructure provider Fireworks to access Cursor data and credentials. The source does not detail how many users were affected.

headline: Trigram campaign impersonates about 50 AI and blockchain brands to trick developers into running infostealers
summary: Stormshield reports a large-scale campaign, named Trigram, that impersonates around 50 AI and blockchain brands. It tricks developers into running an infostealer themselves. Targets include the AI, blockchain and logistics sectors in Europe and the US.

headline: Apache patches critical Roller RCE flaw reported as exploited in attacks
summary: Apache has released updates for a critical flaw in the Roller blogging server that allows remote code execution. The report says threat actors are exploiting it to run code on vulnerable servers. The source gives no CVE identifier.

headline: Apache reports active exploitation of critical Apache Roller vulnerability
summary: The Apache Foundation says attackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in the Apache Roller blogging platform. The source summary does not give the CVE or technical details, and users are urged to update.

headline: Optimizely flaw, dubbed OPTIMJACK, exposed visitors to at least 178 organizations' websites to malicious JavaScript
summary: ReversingLabs reports that a vulnerability in Optimizely let malicious code reach visitors to websites of at least 178 organizations through trusted third-party JavaScript. The research shows a blind spot in how organizations trust third-party scripts. The excerpt does not name the affected organizations or give a CVE.

headline: NSA's classified NSANet network suffers outage, defense official says
summary: A defense official says an outage disrupted NSANet, the National Security Agency's classified internal network. The source does not give a cause and does not say whether a cyberattack was involved.

headline: Tails temporarily removes uBlock Origin in emergency patch over critical XSS flaw
summary: The developers of the privacy-focused Tails operating system issued an emergency update that temporarily removes the uBlock Origin ad blocker. The reason is a critical cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw in the extension.

headline: Google Chrome 158 released with fixes for 204 vulnerabilities
summary: Google released Chrome 158, which fixes 204 security flaws. Google has paid $11,000 in bug bounties for five externally reported bugs, and payouts for 36 others are still to be decided. The source mentions no exploitation.

headline: Huntress analyses EvilTokens, Knight Office and Kali365 phishing kits that steal Microsoft 365 sessions
summary: Huntress researchers describe how three phishing kits capture Microsoft 365 tokens and replay them to hijack sessions. The analysis includes guidance on detecting and containing these attacks.

headline: Cloud credentials leaked in public Docker Hub images are exploited within seconds
summary: Research shows attackers pull cloud keys and secrets out of public Docker Hub images and abuse them within as little as eight seconds of publication. Any secret pushed to a public image should therefore be treated as compromised straight away.

headline: Google: Russian actor Star Blizzard shifts focus to cloud identities for data theft
summary: New Google analysis says Russian espionage group Star Blizzard, also known as Cold Relic, is increasingly compromising cloud environments to steal data in bulk. The access is also used to enable further attacks. The source names no specific targets.

headline: OpenJDK HotSpot compiler vulnerability CVE-2026-114941 published
summary: Amazon Linux lists CVE-2026-114941, a flaw in the OpenJDK HotSpot compiler component. The listing gives no severity and does not say whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: OpenJDK HotSpot runtime vulnerability CVE-2026-114943 published
summary: Amazon Linux lists CVE-2026-114943, a flaw in the OpenJDK HotSpot runtime component. The listing gives no severity and does not say whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: OpenJDK java.lang vulnerability CVE-2026-114945 listed in Amazon Linux CVE index
summary: The Amazon Linux Security Center lists CVE-2026-114945 in the OpenJDK core-libs/java.lang component. The record gives no severity, exploitation status, Amazon Linux affected status or patch availability.

headline: OpenJDK java.lang.management vulnerability CVE-2026-114944 listed in Amazon Linux CVE index
summary: The Amazon Linux Security Center lists CVE-2026-114944 in the OpenJDK core-svc/java.lang.management component. The record gives no severity, exploitation status, Amazon Linux affected status or patch availability.

summary: The Amazon Linux Security Center lists CVE-2026-114947, a vulnerability in the OpenJDK security-libs/javax.net.ssl (TLS) component. The record gives no severity, exploitation status, Amazon Linux affected status or patch availability.

headline: Microsoft research shows device code phishing can extend to AI coding agents such as GitHub Copilot CLI
summary: Microsoft lab research describes how device code phishing works against any device-flow client and can be used against AI coding agents. GitHub Copilot CLI serves as the example. The source does not report any in-the-wild exploitation.

headline: CVE-2026-114939 disclosed in OpenJDK JGSS security library
summary: An Amazon Linux CVE record lists a vulnerability in the OpenJDK security-libs/org.ietf.jgss component, which handles GSS-API/Kerberos authentication. The record gives no severity or impact details and does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: CVE-2026-114940 disclosed in OpenJDK javax.net.ssl TLS library
summary: An Amazon Linux CVE record lists a vulnerability in the OpenJDK security-libs/javax.net.ssl component, which provides Java's TLS support. The record gives no severity or impact details and does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: CVE-2026-114942 disclosed in OpenJDK core-libs component
summary: An Amazon Linux CVE record lists a vulnerability in the OpenJDK core-libs component. The record gives no severity or impact details and does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: CVE-2026-114946 disclosed in OpenJDK HotSpot compiler component
summary: An Amazon Linux CVE record lists a vulnerability in the OpenJDK hotspot/compiler component. The record gives no severity, impact or affected versions, and it does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: Commercial 'TheMailer' phishing kit uses attacker-supplied AI models to personalize and scale lures
summary: Researchers describe TheMailer, a commercial phishing kit that uses AI models supplied by the attacker. The models personalize lures and help them get past spam filters. The kit can scale campaigns to tens of thousands of targets. The source does not name specific victims.

headline: UK National Audit Office finds government risk management falling short
summary: A report from the UK National Audit Office says weaknesses in risk management across government are leading to poor decisions. The source summary does not say how far cyber risk specifically is covered.

headline: Researchers take over Hugging Face account for widely used Kokoro text-to-speech model
summary: Researchers took control of the Hugging Face account for Kokoro, a text-to-speech model, because the platform lacked ownership verification. The model is reportedly used in projects from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and AWS. The source does not report any malicious exploitation, but the case shows a supply-chain risk for AI models.

headline: Physical attack resets TPM lockout, letting short Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs be guessed
summary: Researchers at TU Berlin say someone who opens the case of an AMD-based PC, or of some Intel-based PCs, can reset the TPM anti-hammering lockout. That makes it practical to guess short Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs. In lab tests, they recovered a four-digit Hello PIN and a six-digit BitLocker PIN.

headline: Entrust identity fraud report: document fraud leads, virtual cameras used to defeat face checks
summary: Entrust's latest identity fraud report finds document fraud is still the largest attack category, though its rate fell 19% year over year. Physical counterfeits made up most fraudulent document submissions. Fraudsters are also using virtual cameras to inject faces into identity verification checks.

headline: Canonical offers Ubuntu Pro users AI-generated security patches through opt-in Edge channel
summary: Canonical's AI system, Surge, writes fixes for known vulnerabilities in Ubuntu's userspace software, meaning everything outside the kernel. Ubuntu Pro customers can install these patches early through an opt-in channel called the Edge archive, before Canonical's engineers finish reviewing and testing them. Regular security updates are unchanged for anyone who leaves Edge switched off.

headline: Google reports Chinese state group developing automated AI attack tool for espionage
summary: Google's latest AI Threat Tracker report says a Chinese state group is developing an automated attack tool for cyber espionage. The report says threat actors increasingly use autonomous multi-agent offensive frameworks such as Artex, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI and PentAGI to run multi-stage intrusions faster.

headline: Healthcare organizations struggle to monitor AI tools as shadow AI begins to contribute to breaches
summary: The report says healthcare organizations are adopting AI tools faster than their stretched security teams can monitor them. It links unsanctioned shadow AI use to emerging breaches. The source excerpt gives no specific figures or incidents.

headline: Talos examines malware use of public blockchains as resilient C2 dead drops
summary: Cisco Talos describes how malware operators are moving command-and-control away from centralized servers and hardcoded domains toward public blockchain dead drops. Because these networks have no single point of failure, takedowns and domain blocking work less well against them.

headline: BubbleLoader malware trojanizes WinRAR, Windows Media Player and other Windows binaries
summary: ReversingLabs analyzed BubbleLoader, a loader that patches the entry point of legitimate Windows programs and hides its payload inside PNG images. Known host programs include WinRAR, x64dbg, Windows Media Player and the Firefox launcher. Samples date back to February 2026 and fall into two clusters.

headline: Talos tracks suspected North Korea-aligned UAT-12643 using blockchain infrastructure for infostealing
summary: Cisco Talos found malicious infrastructure linked to a financially motivated group it tracks as UAT-12643. The group is suspected to be North Korea-aligned and combines blockchain-based resilience with targeted infostealing. The source summary does not name victims or sectors.

headline: Unit 42 analyzes OPTIMJACK supply-chain attack via compromised vendor script
summary: Unit 42 describes the OPTIMJACK supply-chain attack, in which a compromised third-party vendor script exposed the websites that loaded it. The write-up stresses strict segmentation of third-party code. The source excerpt does not give the scale or the victims.

headline: Research finds RCE flaws in Brazilian government-sanctioned digital signature middleware
summary: Researchers report remote code execution flaws in major Brazilian digital-signature and authentication middleware used to sign legal documents. They say the flaws could enable fraud. The source does not mention CVEs or exploitation in the wild.

headline: France attributes connected-refrigerator cyberattacks to Iran; US gives low-confidence backing
summary: France has blamed Iran for cyberattacks involving refrigerators. US intelligence agencies have reportedly reached a low-confidence assessment that also points to Iran, but not to any specific group. Officials said similar attacks elsewhere in Europe may also be linked to Iran, though those investigations are at an early stage.

headline: Microsoft announces Windows Server 2028 with security hardening at Ignite 2026
summary: Microsoft announced Windows Server 2028, its next major server operating system release, at Ignite 2026 and promoted hardened security. The source gives no specific feature or release-date details. This is a product announcement, not a vulnerability.

headline: British national Tyler Buchanan sentenced to six years, last of five US Scattered Spider defendants
summary: The US Department of Justice says British national Tyler Robert Buchanan has been sentenced to six years in prison. He is the last of five defendants to be sentenced in the US Scattered Spider hacking case.

headline: Researchers claim two RCE bypasses of Telegram's new Android widget defenses
summary: The security company NebuSec says a malicious bot widget can bypass a security filter that Telegram recently added to its Android app and run code outside it. The demonstration ran on a Telegram test server, because only approved bots can send widgets in production. No exploitation in the wild has been reported.

headline: US court sentences Scottish Scattered Spider defendant to six years in prison
summary: A 24-year-old Scottish man has been sentenced to six years in prison in the United States for his role in Scattered Spider attacks. He is the last of five defendants in the US case to be sentenced.

headline: Anthropic shortens vulnerability disclosure deadline to 30 days for high and critical bugs
summary: Anthropic will publicly disclose high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities it reports to vendors and maintainers after 30 days instead of 90, and all other bugs after 45 days. The change covers reports sent on or after January 1, 2027. The company says AI-driven discovery makes long private embargoes unrealistic.

headline: Suspected Chinese APT rebuilds EggStreme malware and infrastructure after Bitdefender exposure
summary: Bitdefender exposed the EggStreme malware, and a suspected China-linked APT group has since rebuilt both the malware and its infrastructure. The source names no targets or new technical details.

headline: British Scattered Spider leader sentenced to six years in US prison
summary: A British leader of the Scattered Spider cybercrime collective has been sentenced in the United States to six years in prison. The charges covered stealing millions in cryptocurrency and conspiring to hack about a dozen companies.

headline: RIKEN takes Japan's Fugaku supercomputer offline after a security breach
summary: Japan's RIKEN Center for Computational Science has taken the Fugaku supercomputer offline after a security breach. The source excerpt does not give details on the attacker, how they got in, or any data impact.

headline: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer reportedly breached via public status page
summary: A Japanese research centre reports that attackers compromised the Fugaku supercomputer through its publicly accessible status page. The source gives no further details on impact.

headline: Italy extradites Kazakh suspect to US over alleged INC and Lynx-linked ransomware attacks
summary: Italy has extradited Roman Khlynovskiy, a Kazakh national, to the US. US authorities accuse him of taking part in ransomware attacks on healthcare organizations, schools and companies as part of the "8 Digits Team," which is linked to INC and Lynx.

headline: Ipsos investigates breach of an internal system
summary: Market research firm Ipsos has disclosed that it is investigating a breach of an internal system. It made the incident public on 16 November, five days after filing a complaint with the authorities. The scope and impact were not stated.

headline: Tor Project issues emergency relay update during ongoing DDoS attack
summary: The Tor Project has released a security update for its relay software to strengthen defenses against an ongoing DDoS attack. The project says the attack has overwhelmed relays and affected most operators.

headline: GSA says post-quantum pilot on PIV cards shows new encryption can work on legacy technology
summary: The US General Services Administration (GSA) says its post-quantum cryptography work on PIV identity cards shows the new encryption can run on older technology. Officials and contractors are weighing how to adapt legacy systems and how to close gaps in visibility over federal encryption.

headline: CISA acting director says recent tech outages show the need for resilient systems
summary: Nick Andersen, CISA's acting director, says a string of technology outages shows that organizations need to withstand disruptions whether or not a cyberattack causes them. He warned that focus on an AI-fueled "vulnpocalypse" may be crowding out broader resilience planning.

headline: CISA acting director outlines how agency prioritizes critical infrastructure firms for security talks
summary: CISA's acting director, Nick Andersen, described how the agency chooses which critical infrastructure companies to approach first about security improvements. The summary gives no detail on the selection criteria or the sectors involved.

headline: Legal Q&A: can call recordings made 'for training purposes' be used to train AI?
summary: A Dutch legal Q&A column asks whether customer calls recorded "for training purposes" may also be used to train AI models. It raises consent and purpose-limitation questions under privacy law.

headline: Op-ed: US government legacy IT debt framed as a national security risk
summary: A CyberScoop op-ed argues that ageing US federal systems weaken defences against AI-accelerated attacks by foreign adversaries. It says about 80% of federal IT budgets go to maintaining legacy systems.

headline: Researcher warns against running unvetted third-party code on websites
summary: A security researcher argues that organisations underestimate the risk of loading third-party code on their websites. The piece is an awareness-focused commentary and reports no specific incident.

headline: Echo research finds three AI models agree on only one of 121 potential code flaws
summary: Echo ran three AI models (Claude Mythos, GPT-5.6 Sol and GLM-5.3) on the same code and found that their vulnerability findings barely overlapped. Only one of 121 potential flaws was flagged by all three. This suggests AI-assisted code review results are inconsistent and need validation.

headline: External sandbox pattern proposed to isolate code run by AI coding agents
summary: Simon Willison and Prime Radiant published an "external sandbox" pattern: the AI agent runs outside the sandbox, and the code it generates runs inside an isolated one. Three open-source server implementations are available. They include an allow-list proxy that controls which hosts the code can reach, plus a way to make authenticated API calls without giving the agent the secret.

headline: Microsoft makes Perception agentic security platform generally available
summary: Microsoft has made four blue team agents and a Recon Agent in its Perception agentic security platform generally available. Integrations and vulnerability shielding are still in preview.

headline: Deutsche Telekom IoT CEO on long-lived device security and Cyber Resilience Act
summary: In an interview, Deutsche Telekom IoT CEO Christian Schwalbe discusses the risk posed by forgotten IoT devices that stay in service for 15 to 20 years. He also covers what the EU Cyber Resilience Act means for manufacturers, detecting threats from communication patterns without inspecting payloads, and post-quantum cryptography for constrained devices.

headline: Microsoft announces Perception updates and new security stack for AI agents
summary: Microsoft has announced updates to Microsoft Perception and a new Microsoft Security cyber stack. The company says the stack is meant to defend against threats, secure AI agents and protect digital estates. The post is a product announcement and does not report any incident or vulnerability.

headline: Commentary: data privacy and production safety are main concerns with AI pentesting
summary: An industry article argues that AI pentesting can match faster development and exploitation cycles. It says the main concerns are data privacy and safety in production environments rather than the quality of findings.

headline: Researcher says blaming scam victims deepens harm and discourages reporting
summary: At IRISSCON 2026 in Dublin, cyberpsychology researcher Dr. Nicola Fox Hamilton discussed the psychology behind phishing and scams. She argued that blaming victims makes the harm worse and makes them less likely to report future incidents.

headline: Dutch Fraudehelpdesk reports more cases of WhatsApp accounts being taken over
summary: The Dutch Fraudehelpdesk says it is receiving more reports from people whose WhatsApp accounts have been hijacked. The source summary does not say how the accounts are being taken over. Hijacked accounts are often used for impersonation fraud.

headline: Guide lists questions to ask when choosing an AI web application pentesting vendor
summary: A vendor-style checklist offers 15 questions for evaluating AI pentesting providers, focusing on authenticated flows, coverage and production safety. It cites industry figures suggesting that exploitation increasingly starts on or before the day a vulnerability is disclosed.

headline: Apple reports disruptions to iCloud Mail, sign-in, AppleCare and education services
summary: Apple has reported service disruptions affecting several services, including iCloud Mail, iCloud Account & Sign In, Apple School Manager and Schoolwork. The source gives no cause, and nothing indicates a cyberattack.

headline: Dutch consumer regulator ACM releases AI prompt to help consumers check webshop reliability
summary: The Netherlands Authority for Consumers and Markets (ACM) has published an AI prompt that consumers can use to judge whether a webshop is trustworthy. The aim is to help the public avoid fraudulent online shops. It is consumer awareness guidance, not an enterprise threat.

headline: IIHF website defaced with pro-Russian message over Russia's exclusion from competitions
summary: The International Ice Hockey Federation confirmed that its website was attacked. Its homepage was replaced with a pro-Russian message protesting Russia's exclusion from international competitions. The sources do not describe any wider compromise or data theft.

headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models with lower pricing
summary: OpenAI released two new models in its API, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. Astra is priced lower than its predecessor, and early reviews of the models are mixed. The release has no direct security implications.

headline: CISO interview: Glow's Patti Degnan on prioritization in security leadership
summary: In a SecurityWeek interview, Patti Degnan, CISO at endpoint security firm Glow, talks about her career. She explains how having her identity stolen in 2006 led her into security, and why deciding what not to do is part of a CISO's job.

headline: Flipper Devices opens crowdfunding for $399 Linux-based Flipper One multi-tool
summary: Flipper Devices, which makes the Flipper Zero, has started a crowdfunding campaign for Flipper One. The new device is a portable Linux computer and networking multi-tool. It is a product launch with no reported security incident.

headline: TapMap open-source tool maps a computer's active network connections
summary: TapMap is a free desktop app that plots a computer's active connections on a world map, using local GeoIP lookups. It links each connection to the application behind it. Its locations are approximate.

headline: iVerify Basic mobile app offers device compromise checks for individuals
summary: iVerify Basic is a consumer app for iOS and Android that scans devices for signs of compromise. It also helps users improve their security and privacy settings. The source is a product showcase.

headline: Phrack issue 73 published with new security research
summary: The hacker magazine Phrack has published issue 73, its first in just over a year, containing a range of new security research. According to the coverage, the issue stresses the human side of hacking.

headline: ACE shuts down Turkish piracy site Dizigom after settlement with operators
summary: The Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment says Dizigom, one of Turkey's largest piracy streaming sites with about 21 million monthly visits, has shut down. The closure follows a settlement agreement with the site's operators.

headline: Datasette Lite rewritten to run the full Datasette app in the browser using service workers and Pyodide
summary: The developer has released a rewrite of Datasette Lite that uses service workers and Pyodide to run the full Python app in the browser. It can load plugins, specific Datasette versions and more than 100 SQLite versions from URL parameters. This is a developer project update with no security incident.

headline: SANS ISC Stormcast podcast for November 17, 2026
summary: SANS ISC published its daily Stormcast podcast episode. The source gives no content details.
